item.title: a short note about accessibility
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Short post: accessibility is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Accessibility shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.
  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: a small guide to accessibility
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
A quick write-up on accessibility, mostly so future me stops relearning it.

why it matters

Accessibility shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: what i learned about accessibility
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Every few months accessibility bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Accessibility shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
